meta.title: qLDPC surgery on a trapped-ion computer

paper.title: Individually addressed logical Pauli measurements by QLDPC surgery on a trapped ion quantum computer

meta.summary: Logical Pauli measurements of single logical qubits inside a qLDPC code block, by surgery with a gadget of seven ancilla qubits, on Quantinuum's H2-2 trapped-ion computer: X̄1 with 0.72% error in one round, below 0.26% in three, and X̄1 then Z̄2 in sequence with 1.12%.
meta.program: The circuits the authors submitted (their Zenodo record), translated gate for gate: Rz as S/S†, Rxy as √X/X, ZZMax as √ZZ, with the detectors and observables that reproduce the paper's verification counts from its published shot data. Observable 0 is the gadget's logical measurement. After the circuit, the `decode_syndrome` system call runs on the decoder core: the compiled union-find decoder reads every measured bit from the board hub and publishes the correction of observable 0, and a one-qubit pulse conditioned on it follows. The paper decodes offline and names real-time decoding on H2 as future work; the twin adds it to show what it takes.
meta.twin: H2 as QCCD Studio models it: a race track of 40 trap zones in one loop with two ions per zone, the program's 27 ions, and four gate zones (the paper's), so at most four gates, measurements or resets at once. Before every MS gate the second ion is split from its zone, shifted round the loop the shorter way to its partner, and merged. The controller is one RISC-Q board at 500 MHz: a laser channel and a cooling channel per gate zone, four transport lanes, a camera core per gate zone that counts the fluorescence of each measured ion, a frame core and the decoder core.
findings: Every operation of all three circuits ran inside its window on the twin: 629 operations of XR1 (602 pulses on the board, the rest Rz frame updates) with 105 ion transports in 6.78 ms, 1079 of XR3 (1044 pulses, 187 transports) in 11.51 ms, 858 of SEQ (836 pulses, 149 transports) in 9.54 ms. Each measurement is its own 120 µs exposure of its gate zone's camera.

The decoder ran in the same Lean run as the circuit: the measured bits reach it a quarter of a microsecond after the last exposure closes, it decodes in 30.5 µs (XR1), 50.1 µs (XR3) and 45.1 µs (SEQ), and the pulse conditioned on observable 0 starts under a microsecond after its result. Against the ion's millisecond operations, real-time decoding on this controller costs well under 1% of a shot.

Under the paper's own simulation model the twin's logical errors are 1.15% (XR1), 0.35% (XR3) and 1.09% (SEQ) with PyMatching, the 1.0–1.1%, 0.1–0.3% and 0.95–1.06% this model gives, and SEQ matches the paper's simulated 1.000%. The paper's hardware numbers (0.72%, < 0.26%, 1.12%) are on verified shots decoded with Tesseract, a most-likely-error decoder that does better than matching on this qLDPC code.

The paper's error model on these circuits decomposes into a matching graph (Stim splits every error into edges), so the compiled decoder is the graph union-find; its correction equals PyMatching's on all 400 noisy shots of every circuit. On RISC-Q's RTL in Verilator the XR1 decoder commits all 74,989 instructions of 12 decodes on the same cycle as in the Lean model.

The twin's shot (11.5 ms for XR3) is far shorter than the authors' estimate of about 500 ms per shot: sideband cooling before MS gates, leakage repump (about 1 ms a cycle) and the initial cooling (about 17 ms) have no published H2 durations and are not scheduled.
limits: H2's per-operation durations are not public: the twin uses QCCD Studio's H2 model (gates 5 µs and 25 µs, measurement 120 µs, reset 50 µs, split and merge 80 µs, 5 µs per zone), not measured H2 values. Cooling, leakage repump and the initial cooling are not scheduled.
Transport is planned gate by gate (the moving ion goes to its partner's zone and stays there); H2 moves its ions as a conveyor belt, which is not modeled.

The noise is the paper's simulation model (depolarizing gates, preparation and measurement errors, idling per layer) as its verification script states it; the hardware's own errors and leakage are not modeled.

The paper's decoder is Tesseract. The twin's statistics use PyMatching, and the compiled union-find decoder runs on 400 noisy shots, so its own logical error is known only to a few tenths of a percent.

device.title: Quantinuum H2 (QCCD race track), the 27 ions of the program
device.basis: The circuits are the programs the authors submitted (Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.23165109), translated gate for gate (Rz as S/S†, Rxy as √X/X, ZZMax as √ZZ); read back against the published shot data they reproduce the paper's counts and detector rates exactly. H2's per-operation durations are not public: the twin takes QCCD Studio's H2 model (the profile the optical twin uses) and keeps the paper's four gate zones; ions are moved round the race track to their partner before each MS gate. Not scheduled, because H2 publishes no duration for them: sideband cooling before two-qubit gates, leakage repump (about 1 ms a cycle, the paper does not give the number of cycles) and the initial cooling (about 17 ms a shot on H2). That is why a twin shot (about 11.5 ms for XR3) is far shorter than the authors' estimate of about 500 ms. The paper decodes offline (it notes real-time decoding on H2 as future work); the twin adds the decoder and one conditioned pulse in the run, to show what that would take. The controller is a RISC-Q board at 500 MHz: four gate-zone laser channels, four transport lanes, cooling, and readout cores, with a decoder core.

XR1_X1G.source: "A single-round surgery measurement using seven gadget qubits measures the X1 operator with a 0.72 [0.32, 1.41]% (95% credible interval) error rate and agrees with subsequent transversal measurement with 1.03 [0.60, 1.65]% error." (abstract; appendix table tab:results-x1r1: 7/971 verified)

XR3_X1G.source: "For the XR3 gadget circuit, only |++>_L was prepared, with 0 errors in 957 verification passing shots consistent with simulation and upper bounding the error rate at 0.26% in a 95% credible interval." (Sec. IV.A.2)

XR3_unverified.source: "We note that the XR3 error rate depends entirely on the verification step, without verification there are 10 errors in 1000 shots." (Sec. IV.A.2)

XR3_spectator.source: "disagrees in 2/957 verified shots for the three round circuit (error rate 0.21 [0.04, 0.67]%)" (Sec. IV.B.2)

XR3_no_chi_detectors.source: "Decoding without the chi detectors results in 7/957 errors (error rate 0.73 [0.33, 1.43]%)" (Sec. IV.A.2)

SEQ_Z2G.source: "Averaging over preparation in |00>_L and |11>_L the Z2 gadget measurement disagrees with preparation in 11/978 verified shots, with error rate 1.12 [0.60, 1.94]%." (Sec. IV.B.2)

SEQ_sim.source: "with logical error rate 1.000 [0.986, 1.014]%" (Sec. IV.B.2 (simulation, 1e6 shots per preparation))

noise.note: The paper's own simulation model (as its verification script states it): one-qubit 3.4×10⁻⁵, two-qubit 1.0×10⁻³, preparation and measurement 4.7×10⁻⁴ each, and 1.7×10⁻⁵ idling per layer.

exactness: EXACT: gate sequence, gate angles, qubit indices, reset/measure positions — the Stim instruction list equals the QIR instruction list one-for-one (checked in verify.py §2).
EXACT up to global phase: rz/rx/rzz(kπ/2) ↔ Stim S/Z/S_DAG, SQRT_X/X/SQRT_X_DAG, SQRT_ZZ (checked numerically, verify.py §1).
EXACT: measurement record index = QIR %Result id (results are allocated in program order; asserted); output-array position → record index from the result_record_output calls.
DERIVED: TICK placement (sequential packing of program order; the QIR has no layers). TICKs carry no timing.
DERIVED: QUBIT_COORDS(q, 0) = program index on a line; H2 has no fixed qubit geometry (ions are transported).

RECONSTRUCTED from the paper's definitions: detectors and observables. Bulk/boundary/fusion detector rates reproduce the paper's tables tab:fusion and tab:max_rates exactly, and SE1 verification reproduces every post-verification shot count.
INFERRED: the 5-body 'product of all S_Z (S_X) in SE1' detector, added so the detector set spans all deterministic parities and the XR3 count equals the paper's 62.

CHOICE: X1,G uses the chi outcomes of merged cycle 1 (paper Fig. timeline (App. A, fig:gadget_3_round) marks R=1 as the non-destructive measurement); with chi repetition detectors any cycle is equivalent.
NOT EXACT/UNKNOWN: the original pre-TKET Stim circuits are not published (Zenodo has only QIR + results); hardware transport, timing and zone assignment are not public.

decoding.method: offline Tesseract (most-likely-error, search-based) on the Stim detector error model, short-beam configuration
decoding.quote: Decoding is performed offline with the Tesseract most-likely-error decoder acting on the detector error model generated by Stim. ... Specifically, we configure the decoder to the short beam parameters as described in Ref. [Beni2025Tesseract].
decoding.decoder_ref: Aghababaie Beni, Higgott, Shutty, 'Tesseract: A Search-Based Decoder for Quantum Error Correction', arXiv:2503.10988
decoding.statistics_quote: Logical error rates are bounded in equal-tailed 95% Jeffreys credible intervals.
decoding.verification_quote: A logical state of the two encoded qubits is prepared then verified on trivial outcome of the initial bare code syndrome extraction round (SE1).
decoding.here: Tesseract is not installed in this environment (not installed, to leave the environment unchanged); verify.py uses PyMatching (decompose_errors=True works for all DEMs) and a sampled lookup-table decoder as a sanity check.

calibration.decoder: riscq/decoders/uf_decoder.c (union-find with peeling), compiled for a RISC-Q core, Lean model
